required_fixes: Specify Harness continuity when only MCP tokens are refreshed. The pinned engine also receives MCP access tokens only in its one-shot bootstrap (airs_desktop.rs:75-90, airs_desktop_mcp.rs:24-31), so rotating them requires a stop/bootstrap/restore cycle. DESIGN.md:422-469, ADR0003:26-31 and C22 describe that cycle only for the Gateway credential. DESIGN.md:415-416 ('fresh confirmation after a refresh restart') together with :446-448 (decline cancels Send) would also make an MCP-only rotation re-ask WorkspaceWrite and possibly cancel the turn. Working v1 deliberately does the opposite (v1 ADR0031:68-72): before each turn it refreshes the scope's MCP tokens and restarts with an identical context, without SSO refresh or write confirmation. The engine's replay-bound McpServerBinding excludes the grant ID (airs_desktop_mcp.rs:45-52), so engine ContextBinding equality alone cannot detect re-sign-in to a different MCP grant with the same name/server/URL. v1 retires the conversation in that case, while an expired MCP sign-in does not retire it (the non-required server fails startup; ADR0031:56-66). Fix in DESIGN.md/ADR0003/C22 (and W48 if helpful): (a) MCP-only rotation stops and rebootstraps an identical binding and restores compatible history before the explicit turn. State whether WorkspaceWrite is re-asked: either keep v1 (not re-asked) or record a deliberate stricter change with its product impact. (b) Native conversation scope records per-server MCP grant IDs and catalog revisions. Re-sign-in to another grant, sign-out, removal or a revision change retires the conversation even though engine binding equality would pass. (c) Define the expired-MCP-sign-in behavior. (d) Add C22 tests: MCP-only rotation restore with equal binding and no turn replay; WorkspaceWrite behavior on MCP-only restart; same-URL different-grant rejected natively; expired grant leaves the conversation inspectable/sendable per the chosen rule.
